title: If error occurs in `compile_data()`, data context is not deleted
description:
Looking at the code here:
https://github.com/rstudio/sass/blob/d9fe9716de08384797a82f9db945587c0243a35d/src/compile.c#L113-L140

It says:
>  Both context and options return the same `data_context` pointer which is freed by `sass_delete_data_context`

However, in the error code path, `sass_delete_data_context()` never gets called.

title: Test suite failure in connection with language setting
description:
## Describe the problem

When trying to upgrade the Debian packaged sass from version 0.4.8 to 0.4.9 I get a test suite error.
We are using [this test script in our CI](https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-sass/-/blob/master/debian/tests/run-unit-test?ref_type=heads) which finally calls

    LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 R --no-save < testthat.R

This results in the error

    ── Failure ('test-font-objects.R:131:3'): font_collection() basically works ────
    `expect_collection("'foo, bar', baz", quote = FALSE, expected = "'foo, bar', baz")` threw an unexpected warning.
    Message: Changing language has no effect when envvar LC_ALL='C.UTF-8'
    Class:   simpleWarning/warning/condition

      6. │     └─rlang::eval_bare(quo_get_expr(.quo), quo_get_env(.quo))

    [ FAIL 1 | WARN 307 | SKIP 4 | PASS 188 ]

### Session Info

You can find a full build log [here](https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-sass/-/jobs/5696862#L418)

Please let me know if you need further information to track down the issue.  In case you can't reproduce the issue the Debian Med team policy contains a [hint to a docker file](https://med-team.pages.debian.net/policy/#how-to-easily-help-upstream-exactly-reproduce-build-test-errors-that-may-be-specific-to-debian) which could be useful to reproduce the problem on a Debian sid system.

title: Issues with `font_google()` file downloading
description:
Sometime in the last few weeks the Google Fonts API has changed their responses to include hyperlinks with a structure that sass isn't anticipating, which started leading to these unit test failures (since these tests hit an online service, we don't run them on CRAN).

https://github.com/rstudio/sass/actions/runs/8258236915/job/22590137382#step:4:220 

That change in the hyperlink isn't easily reproducible (it seems to happen randomly) and is something we've actually already encountered/addressed in `{bslib}`'s build script to download font files (which happens to use the same approach here in sass)

https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/pull/983
https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/pull/1004

In that last issue, we switched the User-Agent so that we get woff2 (not woff) files, and the problem seems to have gone away (and using woff2 nowadays is likely preferable anyways), so we should do the same. 

As a side effect, by fixing this issue, it should close https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/issues/1000

title: warning: argument unused during compilation: '-stdlib=libc++'
description:
CRAN has requested the following warning be fixed (this is essentially duplicate of https://github.com/rstudio/sass/issues/120)

(Changes should be verified with https://mac.r-project.org/macbuilder/submit.html)

```
* checking whether package ‘sass’ can be installed ... [63s/63s] WARNING
Found the following significant warnings:
   clang: warning: argument unused during compilation: '-stdlib=libc++'
[-Wunused-command-line-argument]

from

clang -falign-functions=8 -g -O2 -Wall -pedantic -Wconversion
-Wno-sign-conversion -Wstrict-prototypes  -O2 -I ./include
-stdlib=libc++ -fPIC -c -o src/cencode.o src/cencode.c
clang: warning: argument unused during compilation: '-stdlib=libc++'
[-Wunused-command-line-argument]

-stdlib-libc++ is (obviously) a C++ option, and the latest Apple Clang
is objecting to its being passed to the C compiler.  You have

sass/src/libsass/Makefile:

ifeq ($(UNAME),Darwin)
         CFLAGS += -stdlib=libc++
         CXXFLAGS += -stdlib=libc++
         LDFLAGS += -stdlib=libc++
endif

where CFLAGS is plainly wrong, and the rest are unneeded for Apple
clang, and potentially wrong if someone chose to use GCC (which has been
done, e.g. by HomeBrew).
```

## Investigation

The primary offending warning is the following (which happens twice, see full install logs below).

```
In file included from src/memory.hpp:9,
                 from src/sass.hpp:55,
                 from src/parser_selectors.cpp:3:
In member function 'void Sass::SharedPtr::decRefCount()',
    inlined from 'Sass::SharedPtr::~SharedPtr()' at src/memory/shared_ptr.hpp:130:18,
    inlined from 'Sass::SharedImpl<Sass::CompoundSelector>::~SharedImpl()' at src/memory/shared_ptr.hpp:195:9,
    inlined from 'Sass::ComplexSelectorObj Sass::Parser::parseComplexSelector(bool)' at src/parser_selectors.cpp:47:7:
src/memory/shared_ptr.hpp:168:15: warning: pointer used after 'void operator delete(void*)' [-Wuse-after-free]
  168 |       --node->refcount;
      |         ~~~~~~^~~~~~~~
```

This warning indicates a use-after-free issue, where the compiler suspects that `node` is referenced after it has been freed. 

AFAICT, the warning happens when a `CompoundSelectorObj` goes out of scope at the end of the if/else block in these lines:

https://github.com/rstudio/sass/blob/2f1f152d84c162ccb9aba1c056e3548079d669d9/src/libsass/src/parser_selectors.cpp#L12-L48

We're suspicious in particular that `compound`, which is created in an `if()` expression, is being flagged:

https://github.com/rstudio/sass/blob/2f1f152d84c162ccb9aba1c056e3548079d669d9/src/libsass/src/parser_selectors.cpp#L42-L47

At the end of this block, the [`SharedPtr`](https://github.com/rstudio/sass/blob/2f1f152d84c162ccb9aba1c056e3548079d669d9/src/libsass/src/memory/shared_ptr.hpp#L122) destructor is being called (via the [`SharedImpl` generic](https://github.com/rstudio/sass/blob/2f1f152d84c162ccb9aba1c056e3548079d669d9/src/libsass/src/memory/shared_ptr.hpp#L195) which privately inherits from `SharedPtr`).

https://github.com/rstudio/sass/blob/2f1f152d84c162ccb9aba1c056e3548079d669d9/src/libsass/src/memory/shared_ptr.hpp#L129-L131

That destructor simply calls `decRefCount()`, which contains the following.

https://github.com/rstudio/sass/blob/2f1f152d84c162ccb9aba1c056e3548079d669d9/src/libsass/src/memory/shared_ptr.hpp#L163-L183

## Thoughts

* sass vendors [libsass](https://github.com/sass/libsass), to which it applies [a number of patches](https://github.com/rstudio/sass/blob/2f1f152d84c162ccb9aba1c056e3548079d669d9/scripts/patches) to address R CMD Check issues.

* The warning only occurs on Windows for R 4.3+, which may indicate an environment or system-related issue.

* We suspect this is an instance of a [false positive warning in GCC 12](https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=Wuse-after-free).

title: Google font files in directory that Github Pages ignores by default
description:
<!--
Before you file an issue, please upgrade to the latest version of bslib and confirm that the problem persists.

remotes::install_github("rstudio/bslib")
-->


## Describe the problem

When using google fonts, the CSS and woff files are placed in a directory beginning with  an underscore. This is by default ignored by Github Pages when building the site unless a `.nojekyll` file is present.

This is quite difficult to debug - if serving from a `/docs` folder, all one can is see a mysterious 404 error on `font.css` with the file present at the relevant path in the repo. 

Would it make sense to have it placed in a directory not beginning in an underscore, assuming `{bslib}` has control over this?

My YAML header is set as follows, with `{bslib}` installed from Github.

```yaml
output:
  html_document:
    theme:
      version: 5
      bg: "#ffffff"
      fg: "#000000"
      headings_color: blue
      primary: "#0000ff"
      navbar-bg: "#0000ff"
      base_font:
        google: "IBM Plex Sans"
      code_font:
        google: "IBM Plex Mono"
```
The font CSS and woff end up in "site-files/_IBM Plex Mono-0.4.0".

title: 0.2.0: Compilation issues on macOS
description:
Hi, I'm hitting some C++ header issues on macOS Catalina with sass v0.2.0:

My Macs are running R 3.6.3 with clang 7 and gfortran 6.1, as [recommended by CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/tools/).

I have the Xcode command line tools (CLT) installed, as recommended:

```sh
# Full Xcode isn't required, just the command line tools (CLT).

# > xcode-select --help
sudo xcode-select --reset
sudo xcode-select --install

# Software update may be required.
# > sudo softwareupdate --clear-catalog
# > sudo softwareupdate --install --all --restart

xcode-select --print-path
# /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools
```

Current `Makevars` config, following recommendations from [r-macos-rtools](https://github.com/rmacoslib/r-macos-rtools) / [R compiler tools for Rcpp on macOS](https://thecoatlessprofessor.com/programming/cpp/r-compiler-tools-for-rcpp-on-macos/) by @coatless:

```
CCFLAGS=-isysroot /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk
CFLAGS=-isysroot /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk
CXXFLAGS=-isysroot /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk
CPPFLAGS=-isysroot /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk -I/usr/local/include
```

I can build Rcpp, RcppArmadillo, RcppAnnoy, and a number of other packages that depend on Rcpp successfully. I'm specifically failing to compile sass, and only on Catalina currently.

For Mojave, I can run this step first to get sass to compile:

```sh
sudo installer \
    -pkg /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/Packages/macOS_SDK_headers_for_macOS_10.14.pkg \
    -target /
```

Apple dropped support for a similar `macOS_SDK_headers_for_macOS_10.15.pkg` package in Catalina, so there's currently no way to fix the C++ headers like you used to be able to in Mojave.

The expected headers are here, for reference: `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/usr/include`.

Is there a tweak I can apply to my `Makevars` that helps fix this issue?

Proper C++ header support is really becoming a headache on macOS, as Apple tightens down the operating system. I have no such issues on Debian or Fedora with Rcpp.

Best,
Mike

title: sass() discards everything but first element of a character vector of rules
description:
Minimal example:

```r
library(sass)
rules <- c(".foo{color:red}", ".bar{background-color:blue}")
sass(rules)
```

```r
/* CSS */
.foo {
  color: red;
}
```

The issue derives from the fact that `as_sass()` returns the character vector as is, which means `compile_data()` received a character vector here 

https://github.com/rstudio/sass/blob/602c20debb4882d0b399a989fd955da01913270a/R/sass.R#L78

But it appears `compile_data()` is expecting a string:

https://github.com/rstudio/sass/blob/602c20debb4882d0b399a989fd955da01913270a/src/compile.c#L113-L115

title: Release checklist for 0.1.1
description:
Release checklist:

- [x] Create branch labelled v[version]-rc, for example, v1.5.2-rc (the "rc" stands for "Release Candidate").
- [x] Change the DESCRIPTION and NEWS on this branch to change the version number to the desired version for CRAN, e.g. from 1.5.1.9008 to 1.5.2.

- [x] Clean your package directory to remove any extraneous files, including ones that are git-ignored. (Warning, this will delete any unsaved buffers in RStudio! Also, be sure to close RStudio before taking this step!) git clean -xdf .
- [x] Build your package. I (jcheng) personally do it from the Mac command line like this:
PATH=$PATH:/Applications/RStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/pandoc R CMD build [pkgdir]
- [x] Do a sanity check by installing/testing the built package.
- [x] Run R CMD check --as-cran pkg_version.tar.gz both locally and on win-builder. You can also use https://r-hub.github.io/rhub/.
- [x] Read every bullet point in the CRAN Policies document if this is the first release of the package. I usually print it out and check off the items one by one.
- [x] Submit to CRAN via their online form.
- [x] If there are R CMD check warnings that are unavoidable, make sure to explain them in the comments.
- [x] If rejected, make changes on the RC branch and bump the fourth (patch) version component, i.e. 1.5.2.1.

- [ ] On master, change the package version to 1.5.2.9000.

title: Tweaks to `as_sass` semantics
description:
It's really cool that `sass()` allows nested unnamed lists! I would like to make this work:

```r
sass(
  list(
    if (use_theme) theme_options, # A named list
    bootstrap_dependencies, # A list of sass_files
    custom_sass # A string
  )
)
```

This _almost_ works now, but not if `use_theme` is `FALSE`. This is because anywhere a `NULL` is found, it turns into `"null"`:

```r
> as_sass(list(
+   NULL,
+   list(foo = NULL),
+   list(bar = list(NULL))
+ ))
/* Sass */
null
$foo: null;
$bar: null;
```

My position is that the first `NULL` should render as empty string, and the `list(foo=NULL)` should render as `$foo: null;`. The third entry should render as either `$bar: (null);` or `$bar: [null];`.

Once you encounter a named list, the recursion shouldn't be via `as_sass`, but something else--`as_sass_value` perhaps?

| object | as_sass | as_sass_value |
|-----|----|------|
| `NULL` | `""` | `"null"` |
| Unnamed list | Recurse with `as_sass`, collapse with `"\n"` | Recurse with `as_sass_value`, then create (bracketed?) Sass list |
| Named list | Recurse with `as_sass_value`, turn into name/value pairs | Recurse with `as_sass_value`, turn into Sass map |
| Numeric, logical | Throw error | Convert to string |
| String | Identity | Identity |
